name: מְתוּשֶׁלַח
gloss: man of the weapon; or man of the shoot
summary: The son of Enoch and father of Lamech, Noah's grandfather, whose nine hundred and sixty-nine years are the longest life scripture records (Gen 5:21–27; 1Ch 1:3); he is in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luk 3:37, Μαθουσάλα). By the figures of Genesis he died in the year of the flood: he was 187 at Lamech's birth, Lamech 182 at Noah's, and the flood came in Noah's six hundredth year (Gen 5:25, 28; 7:6), which makes 969. The name is two words: מְתוּ, an old form of “man of” (the plural מְתִים “men” is in Deu 2:34, and the same first part is in מְתוּשָׁאֵל, Gen 4:18), and שֶׁלַח, the noun “weapon” (2Ch 23:10) or “shoot” (Sng 4:13). Scripture does not explain the name, so its meaning rests on its form alone.

evidence.note: “Enoch lived sixty-five years and fathered מְתוּשָׁלַח”; after which Enoch walked with God three hundred years (verse 22).
“Methuselah lived a hundred and eighty-seven years and fathered Lamech … and all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.”
Lamech lived a hundred and eighty-two years and fathered a son, Noah.
“Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was on the earth”: 187 + 182 + 600 = 969.
מְתוּשָׁאֵל in Cain's line: the same first element with another second.
מְתִם, “men”: the noun whose construct the first element is taken to be.
שִׁלְחוֹ, “his weapon”: the noun of the second element.

note: BDB files the name under מת (m.ea.ac); it is entered here for its second element, which is spelt exactly as שֶׁלַח (pausal שָׁלַח in Gen 5:21, as with Shelah in Gen 10:24). If a מת entry is written it may want to refer to this one; the key can belong to one only. The first element מְתוּ with its ‑û ending is read as an old construct, on the pattern of מְתוּשָׁאֵל and of names like פְּנוּאֵל; that reading is from the form, not from a statement of scripture. A popular reading “when he dies it shall be sent” (from מוּת and the verb) is not what the pointing gives and is not followed, though his death in the flood year is what the figures yield.
